mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES at t-0w signals a renewed contraction in commuting and city-center visits. That suppresses discretionary trips and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w TRANSIT fell to -59.7 and WORKPLACES to -29.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining below their t-1w levels for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above 10 points while TRANSIT stays below -50, households are substituting toward staying home and making fewer shopping trips. That combination pushes RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 10 points while TRANSIT remains below -50
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w RESIDENTIAL was 12.1 and TRANSIT was -59.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is flat or higher over the next 14 days when RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 and TRANSIT stays below -50.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM after a weak baseline indicates fewer essential errands overall, which usually precedes fewer bundled discretionary outings. That weakens RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w GROCERY_PHARM fell to -10.1 from -6.7 in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains below -6 for most of that period.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT drops by more than 10 points in a week, it marks a fresh mobility shock that quickly reduces access to shopping districts. RETAIL_REC should fall within one week of that threshold being crossed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w TRANSIT declined from -47.0 to -59.7, a 12.7-point fall
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not deteriorate within 7 days after a week with a TRANSIT drop greater than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS activity stays below its recent average while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, households are spending time locally rather than making retail trips. This indoor-within-neighborhood pattern suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w PARKS was -27.4 and RESIDENTIAL was 12.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while PARKS remains below -20 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 10.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in WORKPLACES above its recent trough should restore weekday foot traffic and lunch-hour shopping. That mechanism lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, provided the workplace recovery persists.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 5 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:t-1w WORKPLACES improved to -17.7 from -25.7 before falling to -29.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 28-day mean even after WORKPLACES posts a week-on-week increase of 5 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both rise together, households consolidate trips into essentials and reduce spontaneous retail outings. That co-movement predicts lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w GROCERY_PHARM was -10.1 and RESIDENTIAL was 12.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken over 14 days despite simultaneous increases in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: In a restriction-tightening regime, simultaneous deterioration in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES creates a delayed collapse in discretionary trips that is larger than either series alone. RETAIL_REC should therefore fall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w both series worsened sharply versus t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is unchanged or higher over the next 28 days even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed below their t-0w levels.
